title: Core OOP: Polymorphism & Inheritance
subject: OOPM
aim: To implement runtime polymorphism and method overriding using inheritance in Java / C++.
theory: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to respond to the same method call in unique ways.
procedure: Define a base class Shape with a method draw().
Create derived classes Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle.
Override draw() in each derived class.
Create objects of the derived classes.
Invoke draw() to observe polymorphism.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to achieve method overriding in Java?

result: Dynamic method dispatch correctly invoked the overridden draw() method.
conclusion: Polymorphism allows flexible and reusable class interfaces.

title: Interface
subject: OOPM
aim: To understand and implement interfaces in Java.
theory: An interface in Java is a blueprint that defines methods which implementing classes must provide.
procedure: Create an interface named Animal.
Declare a method sound() inside the interface.
Create a class Dog that implements the Animal interface.
Implement the sound() method in the Dog class.
Create an object of Dog and call the sound() method.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to implement an interface in Java?

result: The interface was successfully implemented by the Dog class.
conclusion: Interfaces provide abstraction and define a common contract for implementing classes.

title: Package
subject: OOPM
aim: To understand and implement packages in Java.
theory: A package in Java is used to group related classes and interfaces.
procedure: Create a  named mypackage.
Create a Calculator class inside the package.
Define an add() method in the Calculator class.
Import the Calculator class from the package.
Create an object and call the add() method.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to import a class from a package in Java?

result: The Calculator class was successfully imported from the package.

title: Exception
subject: OOPM
aim: To understand and implement exception handling in Java.
theory: Exception handling is used to handle runtime errors and maintain the normal flow of a program.
procedure: Write a try block containing the statements that may cause an exception.
Create an arithmetic operation that causes division by zero.
Use a catch block to handle the ArithmeticException.
Display a message after handling the exception.

questions.question: Which block is used to handle an exception in Java?

result: The ArithmeticException was successfully handled using the catch block.
conclusion: Exception handling helps prevent abnormal program termination and allows errors to be handled properly.

title: Multithreading
subject: OOPM
aim: To understand and implement multithreading in Java.
theory: Multithreading allows multiple threads to execute concurrently within a program.
procedure: Create a class that extends the Thread class.
Override the run() method.
Create an object of the thread class.
Call the start() method to begin thread execution.
Observe the execution of the thread.

questions.question: Which method is used to start a thread in Java?

result: The thread was successfully created and started.
conclusion: Multithreading allows multiple tasks to execute concurrently and improves program efficiency.

title: File Handling

aim: To understand and implement file handling in Java.
theory: File handling in Java is used to create, read, write, and manage files using classes such as File, FileWriter, and FileReader.
procedure: Create a file using Java file handling classes.
Open the file for writing.
Write data into the file.
Close the file.
Observe the file operation result.

questions.question: Which class is commonly used to write data to a file in Java?

result: Data was successfully written to the file.
